paper_id: NL2Lean_ Translating Natural Language into Lean 4 through Multi-Aspect Reinforcement Learning
title: NL2Lean: Translating Natural Language into Lean 4 through Multi-Aspect Reinforcement Learning
motivation: Writing accurate formal Lean 4 requires deep familiarity with syntax and logical rules, placing significant burden on domain experts.
problem_framing: LLMs rely on instruction tuning and lack fine-grained structural and semantic alignment, producing syntactically and logically incorrect formal proofs.
key_insight: Four reward signals (semantic, term-level, global-level, compile-check) combined with multi-aspect curriculum learning from easy to hard progressively improves translation quality.
method_signature: Multi-aspect RL framework with dense rewards + curriculum learning on PPO-optimized LLaMA-8B base translator.
evaluation_criteria: Compile rate + semantic faithfulness judged by backtranslation comparison and human annotators.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Compile-checking reward achieves high compilation (19.3%) but limited semantic accuracy (15.6%), confirming syntactic validity alone is insufficient.
evidence_for_taste: syntactic validity alone is not sufficient
time-consuming, expensive, and difficult to scale
thinking_moves: 把形式化问题分解为多个正交评估维度而非单一指标
